claims.text: SMAT applied to CoCrFeNi produces a gradient ultrananocrystalline surface layer.
The SMAT-produced layer dynamically evolves into a self-healing lubricious glaze during sliding.
The resulting glaze maintains low friction and wear from room temperature to 800 °C.
Conventional coarse-grained CoCrFeNi exhibits variable tribological performance at elevated temperatures.
A controlled SMAT treatment can induce a graded ultrananocrystalline surface layer in CoCrFeNi.
Sliding-induced stress transforms the graded nanocrystalline layer into a shear-localized protective glaze.
The SMAT-induced nanostructure is predisposed to dynamic amorphization during sliding.
Dynamic amorphization facilitates continuous formation and regeneration of a lubricious glaze.
The regenerated glaze mitigates adhesive and oxidative wear across a wide temperature range.
SMAT-treated CoCrFeNi will have a lower coefficient of friction than untreated CoCrFeNi.
The coefficient of friction of SMAT-treated CoCrFeNi will approach or fall below approximately 0.3.
SMAT-treated CoCrFeNi will have significantly lower wear rates than untreated CoCrFeNi.
The improved tribological performance will persist near 800 °C.
Untreated coarse-grained CoCrFeNi has inadequate friction and wear resistance at elevated temperatures.
Optimized SMAT will be effective from room temperature to 800 °C under the tested loads and atmospheres.
Performance may change substantially when SMAT parameters or test conditions depart from their optimized values.
The uniformity and reproducibility of nano-glaze formation may depend on SMAT parameters.
Ball-on-disk tests comparing treated and untreated CoCrFeNi across temperature, load, and atmosphere can test the hypothesis.

Failure to achieve a statistically significant friction reduction, with friction remaining above approximately 0.3, together with failure to form a stable self-healing glaze across the full temperature range would falsify the hypothesis.
